newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges grain enterprises to reduce losses.
newsitem.headline: China urges grain enterprises to reduce losses.

text.p: Chinese authorities have ordered grain departments at all levels to improve management to reduce losses by the end of this year, officials and state media said on Wednesday.

The target set by the Internal Trade Ministry and the State Grain Reserve Administration was to reduce losses in the first 10 months of this year with a campaign to recover 2.0 billion yuan ($240 million) in the last two months of the year, a ministry official said by telephone.
He said the losses in the first 10 months were enormous but declined to elaborate.
Bad business management was an important factor in serious losses at grain enterprises, the newspaper quoted internal trade minister Chen Bangzhu as saying.
He said enterprises must set up good internal financial systems and strive to turn losses into profits.
Grain authorities had issued regulations to tighten control of funds used for state purchase of grain, the newspaper said.
Under the regulations, enterprises and grain officials that receive funds earmarked for state purchasing are banned from using the money for other purposes, it said.
A large proportion of China's grain crop is still bought by the state at prices well below market levels, creating money-making opportunites for unscrupulous officials.
China has said it expects to produce a grain harvest of 475 million tonnes this year, up from a record 466 million in 1995.
